title: Fayol's Rules for Running a Team | Principles of Management Ep 9
description:
Chai Corner has six people now, but Asha gets opposite orders from Ravi and Kabir, two helpers wash the same cups, and nobody counts the money. In this animated lesson we use Ravi's chai stall to understand Henri Fayol's administrative management, step by step.

You will meet Henri Fayol, the French mining engineer who took over a company close to going bust in 1888, ran it for thirty years, and wrote Administration industrielle et generale in 1916. We see his six kinds of work in every company, then watch Ravi run one busy Saturday through Fayol's five functions: planning, organising, commanding, coordinating and controlling. We sort all 14 principles of management into four simple groups, and see what division of work, unity of command, the scalar chain with its gang plank, equity and esprit de corps look like in a hospital, an office and a sales team today. We also look at the limits honestly: the rules see work from the top, and in 1946 Herbert Simon said some of them clash like old proverbs.

This is Episode 9 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
